items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: Manuel had his band on there, Joe had his band, see, well, because we used to work, we were the Superior band, see, when Superior band go, off on gigs, we work in there

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. I remember when they began...
I was so wrong, I had a right to those people. I heard that, Joe. It wasn't a thing wrong with me. And I wrote down there and had them straighten that thing out.

items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: We had Eddie Atkins and Duterte. King Oliver.

ctx.x: Why did your brother play? Violin. What's his first name? Willie. Willie. Willie Foster. Yeah. I had Eddie Atkins. First we had Eddie Atkins.

We had Duterte for a while. We had Eddie Atkins and Duterte. King Oliver. Uh-huh. King Oliver. Uh-huh. Piku. Uh-huh. Had a guy called Chris. I never know what Chris's last name. Blaine Drum. Myself. Louis Kepp played guitar. We had a good band. Did you have some kind of a uniform? Yeah.
Yeah. And a guy with a uniform?

items.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: And King Oliver and my brother, man, they boys hit me for a long time. Don't eat that, man.

ctx.x: And I said, Louie, did you get them?

Yeah. I said, Louie, did you get them? Yeah. I said, well you had two. I went to the toilet, I stopped the toilet. See I couldn't go. Once I go in the cavalry, I had to stay in there. Because the cops would chase me. Because I was underage, I ain't got no business down there. But my boys being a good family. You're supposed to be 21 to work there, huh? Yeah. See I could go on one side of the street, but the cops on this corner knowed me. See you had two cops here, two cops here, two cops over there, two cops over…

Oh yeah? Well let's, let's, well you know, we can all join in. Yeah. How did you first start, Rosie? Well I started on Clark Street, Chicago, just when I was a kid going to school. Are you a, are you a Chicagoan? Yes, I'm born and raised in Chicago. I didn't know the north side. Everyone thinks I was raised in the south side, but I wasn't. It'd be right up south side. I used to live on the south side and I had music, Joe Alvarez. Who were the first people you heard on the south side? Joe Alvarez. Joe Alvarez. No,…
